newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian premier seeks tough move on oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian premier seeks tough move on oil prices.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Thursday that his government needed to take a bold decision to contain a high oil pool deficit arising out of subsidised fuel prices.

"That is unavoidable," he said in response to a question on the oil deficit during an interview on state-run Doordarshan television. "It is an unfortunate part of government that sometimes bold decisions will have to be taken," he said.
Gujral said he would need the nation's support and confidence in tackling the huge oil pool deficit.
"You cannot go on living with this kind of deficit that you are soon reaching a stage where you do not have the money to buy. I do not want to reach that stage," Gujral said.
"We will try to soften the blow as much as we can," the prime minister said.
Analysts say pressure was mounting on the government to raise prices of petroleum products to tackle the burgeoning oil pool deficit.
India's oil pool account reconciles the state-fixed administered pricing mechanism with free market conditions.
The oil pool account is a balancing mechanism whereby refineries are compensated for subsidised prices of several petroleum products in India.
The oil pool account for 1996/97 (April-March) is estimated to be running a deficit of 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion).
India's demand for petroleum products is forecast to go up to about 81 million tonnes in the year ending March 31, 1997 from 74.7 million in 1995/96.
India imported 47.68 million tonnes of crude oil and petroleum products in 1995/96.
